hook: The Norse cosmos was never mapped, yet we try to build it.

sections.voiceover: The Norse cosmos was never mapped, yet we try to build it.
sections.visual_cue: Abstract geometric lines forming a tree structure on a dark background.

sections.voiceover: In 2024, the Worlds of Valhalla project opened in Reykjavik as a 1225 square meter immersive experience. How do we visualize a world with no complete map?
sections.visual_cue: Architectural floor plan of the 1225 square meter exhibition space in Reykjavik.
b_roll: Floor plan of the Worlds of Valhalla exhibition
Manuscript illustration of the world disc

sections.voiceover: The Seiðr Loom research project notes that no medieval text lists all nine worlds.
sections.visual_cue: Text overlay highlighting the discrepancy between modern installations and medieval records.

sections.voiceover: Designers Aron Þór Leifsson and Tobia Zambotti utilized Gagarín, a design firm, for this interpretation. This project attempts to anchor Yggdrasil, the cosmic tree, in a 3D space.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of digital design software rendering 3D nodes of the World Tree.

sections.voiceover: Gagarín's 1225 square meter installation now shapes how we perceive the ancient Norse universe today.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the exhibition installation fading into an old Norse manuscript page.
